summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of kidney transplantation was admitted with fever, dysuria, and suprapubic pain one week after completing IV antibiotics for multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. She was found to have a recurrent MDR Klebsiella urinary tract infection with mild leukocytosis and acute kidney injury (creatinine 1.6). Imaging showed stable transplant kidney and bilateral atrophic native kidneys without hydronephrosis. She was treated with IV meropenem and showed clinical improvement, becoming afebrile with normalization of white blood cell count and creatinine returning to baseline (1.0). She was transitioned to outpatient IV ertapenem for a 14-day course via a midline with visiting nurse support. Plans include urology follow-up for urodynamic studies, transplant ID consultation for long-term suppression, and continuation of diabetes management with her insulin pump. She was discharged home in stable condition.
